objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A village relic stupa: a stepped square terrace with three-step redented corner piers and one round-headed arched aedicule per face, a round stone plinth, a bell dome on a moulded foot, a square harmika cube seated into the dome under a wider cornice cap, a sixteen-ring conical taper and a worn gilt needle finial. The registry notes name the readable feature exactly -- "stepped square base, rounded bell, ringed taper, needle spire" -- and every authoring decision here serves that profile rather than any surface.

reasoning: Silhouette is the whole subject and it is NOT simple: bell, ringed taper and needle are three different curvatures stacked on a stepped square, and the registry notes say that profile must survive at a distance where no surface detail is visible at all.
Component count is low on purpose. Every ring, moulding and step is a PROFILE POINT rather than a mesh, so richness costs triangles -- the axis with headroom -- instead of draw calls.
Occlusion risk is unusually low for this kit: the prop is four-fold symmetric, so the single plate showing two of the four faces effectively shows all of them.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, cylinder collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Profile-dominated rather than repetition-dominated, which is the opposite of the retail set. The one repeating element is the four arched aedicules, and they must be repetitionSystems: as four separate frames plus four separate back panels they would cost eight draw calls of the twelve available, for four copies of two geometries.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 7.00 x 14.00 x 7.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; cylinder collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as CYLINDER rather than the building-part default box, and the asset notes give the reason: the bell and spire are round in plan, so a box proxy would leave a player colliding with empty air at the corners for eight of the prop's fourteen metres. The shipped physics compound is a HAND-PLACED eight-part stack in colliders.json (four terrace boxes, the niche storey as a cross, two bell cylinders, one harmika box), measured at coverage 0.975 and overshoot 0.054.

silhouette.description: Read bottom to top: a bottom slab to 0.55, three plinth steps to 1.22, the niche storey to 2.75 with its aedicules standing proud to 3.43, two cornice courses stepping OUT to 3.22 m half-width by 3.12, an upper slab at 2.77 to 3.30, a round stone plinth at 2.63 m radius; a stucco foot band (2.58) and waist (2.28); a BELL whose body rises from 2.36 m radius at 4.15 to 1.90 at 6.40 and rounds over a domed shoulder (1.58 at 7.15, 1.28 at 7.40, 0.93 at 7.62, 0.71 at 7.87) into a 1.46 m harmika cube seated in the dome from 7.45, capped by a cornice stepping out to 1.84 m and a 1.68 m top slab to 8.93; a sixteen-ring conical taper from 0.62 m radius at 8.85 to 0.20 at 12.30; a gilt needle to 14.00. The silhouette events are the terrace steps, the round plinth turning the square base into the round bell, the bell's flank turning into its dome, the harmika's square interruption with its wider cap, and the needle. Every radius above the terrace is the Meshy proxy's own radius-by-height at 56 slices, scaled to the declared 14 m; the terrace half-widths and redents are fitted to the proxy's per-slice corner reach (r95) and face reach (halfX) together.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z both span -3.50..+3.50 = 7.00, set by the bottom terrace slab: its redented plan has its widest point on the flat of each face at 3.50, and the three corner redents cut INWARD from there, so the corners do not push the bounding box out past the faces. y spans 0.00 (terrace underside) to 14.00 (finial tip). Nothing else reaches any of those planes -- the aedicules stand proud to 3.43 and the bell to 2.63 -- so the envelope is set by exactly two parts. The footprint was RE-DECLARED 8 -> 7 m for this build: the Meshy proxy scaled to the kept 14 m has halfX 3.42-3.50 on every slice from 0 to 2.9 m (scratch/_mon/profile.mjs, 56 slices), i.e. w:h = 0.50, and a plate solve on the bottom slab edges gives 6.2-6.6 m; the old 8 m built a squat pyramid the plate does not show.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 2.000 : 1.000 against the ORIGINAL declaration of 1 : 1.750 : 1.000 -- depth exact, height 14% taller. The declared 14 m is kept and the footprint is re-declared to the proxy's: at 14 m its terrace halfX is 3.42-3.50 on every slice from 0 to 2.9 m, so w = d = 7.0. Area-weighted band comparison against the reference mesh (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs) now gives mean |delta width| 0.012 and |delta depth| 0.011 of height, bands 3-9 (everything above the terrace) within 0.010 and the residual entirely in bands 0-1, where the 5-95 percentile of a redented terrace is dominated by which slab tops are widest and reads the candidate 0.04 narrow. The second build measured 0.019 with band 3 at +0.044 and band 5 at +0.032.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED, but confidence is 0.80 rather than the 0.20 this kit gives an unseen elevation: the prop is four-fold symmetric about its axis, so the rear faces are the same faces as the two the plate shows. What is genuinely unknown is only whether the real object's four niches differ from one another.

componentTree.name: Stepped terrace
componentTree.topologyRationale: Eight stepped slabs and the round plinth under the bell in one material and ONE merge. Each slab is a single EXTRUSION of a closed three-step redented plan rather than a wide box crossed by a deep one: crossed boxes put their top faces in the same plane facing the same way over the whole intersection, which z-fights, and one closed plan has no interior coincidence at all. The plinth is a lathe whose open rim runs up inside the bell's stucco foot band.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Eight redented slabs from y=0.00 to y=3.30 -- half-widths 3.50, 3.42, 3.32, 3.20, the 3.00 niche storey (1.22-2.75), cornices 3.12 and 3.22, upper slab 2.77 -- with redents of 0.22 to 0.37 deepening with height, fitted to the proxy's per-slice r95 and halfX; then a round stone plinth at 2.63 m radius from 3.20 to 3.46 with a lip.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Consecutive slabs meet as OPPOSED faces -- one slab's top against the next slab's bottom -- which is how solids are meant to meet and does not fight. check-coplanar reports the prop clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is recorded as "extrusion" because that is what each slab is; the eight slabs and the plinth lathe are MERGED into one BufferGeometry and ONE draw call.

componentTree.name: Bell dome
componentTree.topologyRationale: A surface of revolution, so a lathe is the only honest primitive: a box decomposition of a bell is not a low-poly bell, it is a different object. The foot band, the waist and the neck under the harmika are PROFILE POINTS on the same lathe, not separate meshes, which is what keeps the whole dome at one geometry and one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: One lathe from y=3.45 to y=8.25 at 40 segments: a torus band at 2.58, a waist at 2.28, a body from 2.36 at 4.15 to 1.90 at 6.40, the dome through the proxy's 1.75 (6.90), 1.58 (7.15), 1.28 (7.40), 0.93 (7.62), 0.71 (7.87) and 0.60 (8.05) run through a Catmull-Rom at 26 steps, then a 0.55 m neck to 8.25 inside the harmika cube. Every radius is the Meshy proxy's radius-by-height at 56 slices.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The lathe's open bottom rim (2.50 at 3.45) is INSIDE the stone plinth ring (2.63 to 3.46), and its open top rim is inside the harmika cube, which is seated down into the dome from 7.45 -- its corners meet the dome surface at 7.57 and its face centres at 7.85. LatheGeometry is open at both ends; an open rim sitting exactly on a surface is a seam the turntable gate can read through.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-terrace (PBR confidence 0.860). Textureless as far as the GENERATOR is concerned: no five-canvas procedural set, which would discard this measurement since the generator forces color to white whenever one exists. The crazing, soil and joint moss are a post-construction Canvas 2D tile bound as map and bumpMap, a multiplier on this measured colour, see localOverride d11-lichen-crazing.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Five components and two repetition systems: 7 of 12. The lever here is the LATHE and the merge: every moulding, ring and step is a profile point rather than a mesh, and the eight slabs plus the round plinth are one geometry, so the sixteen spire rings, the foot mouldings and the terrace cost one draw call each.

materials.note: stucco covers the bell, the harmika AND the spire -- three components, one material, because they are the same whitewash. The round plinth under the bell is STONE and rides on the terrace merge, so the material boundary between the square base and the round bell costs nothing. Four of eight materials, four in hand.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are where this prop spends, and deliberately: 8,312 of 16,000, most of it in the two lathes (the bell at 40 segments through a 47-point profile, the spire at 24 through 50). That is the correct trade for a subject whose entire identity is its profile, and the headroom must not be read as room to split components -- draw calls are the scarce axis.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Lathes and extrusions, not boxes. A bell, a ringed taper and a needle are surfaces of revolution and a box decomposition of one is not a low-poly version of it but a different object; the terrace is an extruded redented plan for the same reason -- crossed boxes would z-fight where they intersect. The only boxes on the prop are the harmika's four and the niche back panels.
Two InstancedMesh systems carry 8 of the prop's 13 discrete parts, all four-fold symmetric about the axis.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless to the GENERATOR -- no five-canvas procedural set. Two Canvas 2D wear tiles (peel/crazing on the stucco, crazing/joint-moss on the stone) are drawn post-construction as a few hundred Path2D fills at 512 px and bound as map and bumpMap, the route the retail set uses for its fascias; no per-pixel JavaScript, and the measured albedo stays on the material as the multiplicand. The factory builds in ~70 ms with 2.7 MB of texture VRAM; under Node, with no DOM, the materials keep their flat measured colour.

risks.description: The plate's own proportions read closer to 12.5 m at this width, and Meshy reads it taller still at 16 m.
risks.mitigation: The declared 14 m is between the two and the registry notes call it correct for a village chedi; the footprint now follows the proxy at that height (7 m), so the proportions are the proxy's even if the absolute size is the declaration's.

risks.description: The peel and crazing are a 3 m tile, so the same flake recurs round the bell about four times; the stone tile repeats on every terrace face.
risks.mitigation: The tile is seeded and seamless, holds one large flake and three small ones, and at the distance a 14 m landmark is read the repeat is below notice. The alternative -- a projected plate crop -- would need the texture set that discards every measured albedo, and this prop is four-fold symmetric anyway.

risks.description: The stone tile's moss bands are keyed to world height on the vertical faces; on the up-facing ledges the box projection reads v from z, so the same bands cross the ledge tops as stripes at unrelated positions.
risks.mitigation: The ledges are 0.10-0.20 m wide and carry the 0.76 top tint; a stripe crossing one reads as moss on a ledge, which the plate has, and the aedicule frames take the bands at the same real heights as the wall behind them.

risks.description: The plate's shaded bell flank reads 116 against a lit 208 (0.56); the harness renders the same flank at 156 against 191 (0.82), so the bell models flatter than the plate whatever the albedo.
risks.mitigation: Recorded, not authored around: darkening the albedo to hit the shaded value would render the lit face beige, which was the second build's fault.

risks.description: All four aedicules are authored the same; the plate shows two.
risks.mitigation: The prop is four-fold symmetric and the two visible aedicules match. Recorded as an assumption rather than closed silently.
